original_question: Let X^r be the space of C^r vector fields on the sphere. Is every continuous arc in X^r arbitrarily well approximable by a continuous arc that meets only finitely many bifurcation points, meaning finitely many points outside the set of structurally stable vector fields where qualitative changes occur?
target_in_paper: Section 6.2, "The problem of the arc," read together with Section 6.1 for the nearby notation of the structurally stable set and its complement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))
correct_elements: You correctly captured the paper’s target setting (vector fields of class C^r on the sphere), the object under study (a continuous arc in that space), the approximation requirement, and the intended meaning of bifurcation points as encounters with non-structurally-stable vector fields where qualitative changes occur. Your draft is already very close to the wording of the paper’s Section 6.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))
missing_details: The question should explicitly name the subset S of C^r-structurally stable vector fields inside the ambient space X, since Section 6.1 sets up the structurally stable/non-structurally-stable dichotomy used in Section 6.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))

To be fully stand-alone, the topology should be stated: X is considered with its C^r topology, and the approximation of arcs should be understood in the induced C^0 topology on continuous maps into X. The nearby discussion in Section 6.1 is where the topology is made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))

A mathematically sharp standalone version should parametrize an arc as a continuous map from a compact interval, e.g. [0,1], into X; the paper says only "continuous curve (an arc)." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))

The finiteness condition should be stated precisely as finiteness of the set of parameter values t for which the approximating arc lies outside S; the paper describes these as bifurcation points, i.e. points outside the structurally stable set where qualitative changes occur. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))

If one wants notation aligned with the paper, it is better to write X = X^r(S^2) and then distinguish S and X minus S, rather than leaving only the ambient symbol X^r without naming the structurally stable subset. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))
refined_question: Let X = X^r(S^2) be the space of C^r vector fields on the 2-sphere S^2, endowed with the C^r topology, and let S be the subset of C^r-structurally stable vector fields. If gamma:[0,1]→X is a continuous arc, must every neighborhood of gamma in C^0([0,1],X) contain a continuous arc eta:[0,1]→X such that eta(t) lies outside S for only finitely many t in [0,1]? Equivalently: can every continuous arc in X be arbitrarily well approximated by a continuous arc that meets only finitely many bifurcation points, meaning finitely many parameter values at which the arc passes through X minus S?
justification: The draft is plainly targeting Peixoto’s "problem of the arc" in Section 6.2, because it almost paraphrases that statement. I kept the question narrowly on that original approximation problem, rather than replacing it by the later related Peixoto-Newhouse result, since the paper presents the latter only after explicitly saying that the original approximation problem has a negative answer once persistent accumulation of bifurcations is understood. I used Section 6.1 only to make the ambient notation and topology stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1808.10571))

citations.label: Comment on the later negative answer and the Peixoto-Newhouse modification
